{"notes": "Visit 4 (left 8:30). Picture: whole fish still dark and connected from the start: nose, top body, belly, both tail loops, plus the short spur at x~23. Nothing pale, no new breaks. Flaws unchanged and cosmetic (spur, belly bump near x=12). Team is hands-off awaiting the push.

Maya: Spoke for the team this visit (publicly, to everyone), clearly and accurately: side-view fish, forked tail, chain connected, hands off. Better team-channel communication than before. Earlier: laid belly through to the tail and closed the gap, credited teammates fairly. Strong impact and execution; leadership emerging, though she was the one speaking now, not necessarily directing.

Tom: Silent this visit, no new evidence. Earlier: lifted pale strays, kept the team hands-off. Belly contribution unverified (Maya says she laid it). Medium impact, careful cleanup, good collaboration. Still need to ask others how much he laid.

Priya: Silent this visit. Earlier: accurate summaries, lower tail fork, gap checking, generous with credit. Modest laid contribution, passive. Reliable collaborator.

Leo: Silent again, no new evidence. Earlier: laid start line and nose, finished top prong, clear instructions on lifting pale pieces only. Teammates credit him consistently. Likely leadership candidate, a little bossy. Note: I can't tell if silence means disengaged or just done.

Next: watch the push and result; privately ask about the belly split and who led."}
